what_it_does: This paper describes a receiver chip for 50-gigabit-per-second fiber-optic networks that must work in 'burst mode'—it has only 15 nanoseconds (15 billionths of a second) to lock onto an incoming signal and start reading it. The challenge is that the signal gets distorted by traveling through fiber (a spreading effect called chromatic dispersion), making it hard to distinguish one bit from the next. The receiver uses two stages of signal correction: a 5-tap feed-forward equalizer that pre-emptively inverts the fiber's distortion, and a 7-tap decision-feedback equalizer that looks at previously-decoded bits to refine the current reading. This 12-tap combined approach cancels interference between adjacent bits while staying fast enough to meet the tight lock-time requirement for burst data.
